page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What changes
steps.why: The sperm has to be altered inside the female tract before its acrosome can work.
common_mistakes: Calling it a change in shape. The changes are physiological, not structural.
steps.memory_tip: Capacitation gives the sperm the capacity to fertilise.
lines: Capacitation is the set of physiological
changes in the spermatozoa that take place

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.why: Without it the sperm cannot penetrate the egg, so fertilisation cannot happen at all.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the purpose. The second mark is for it.
Writing that it happens in the testis.
steps.memory_tip: Only a capacitated sperm can enter the egg.

lines.text: Only then can a sperm penetrate and fertilise an egg

insider_note: The point is that a freshly ejaculated sperm cannot fertilise. Say so, and the definition earns both marks.
